name: Double Top
description: A pattern forming two consecutive peaks at approximately the same price level, separated by a trough. It signals that buyers failed to push price beyond a resistance level on the second attempt, indicating a potential trend reversal from bullish to bearish.
formation_rules: Price must be in a confirmed uptrend prior to pattern formation
First peak forms as price rallies to a resistance high, then pulls back at least 10% to a trough
Second peak forms as price rallies back toward the first peak high, within 3% of the first peak
The second peak must not exceed the first peak by more than 3%
The trough between the two peaks defines the neckline support level
Time between the two peaks should be at least 2 weeks on daily charts for significance
The pattern spans a minimum of 4 weeks to be considered valid
volume_rules: Volume is typically higher on the first peak than the second peak. Lower volume on the second peak relative to the first is a bearish signal. Volume must expand at least 1.5x average on the neckline breakdown candle for confirmation.
measured_target_method: Measure the vertical distance from the peaks to the neckline trough. Project that distance downward from the neckline breakdown point to get the minimum price target.
confirmation_conditions: Price closes below the neckline (trough low) on a daily candle
Breakout candle volume is at least 1.5x the 20-period average volume
A failed retest of the neckline from below confirms the breakdown
Bearish divergence on RSI between the two peaks strengthens the signal
invalidation_conditions: Price closes above either peak high, negating the double top structure
Price reclaims and closes above the neckline after a confirmed breakdown
The second peak forms on significantly higher volume than the first peak
A bullish engulfing candle forms at the neckline test from below

agent_rules.rule: Breakdown is confirmed only when the closing price is strictly below the neckline (trough low); intraday violations without a close are not valid triggers.
Volume on the breakdown candle must be >= 1.5x the 20-period SMA of volume; record the pattern as unconfirmed if volume threshold is not met.
Pattern is invalidated if price closes above the higher of the two peaks at any point during or after formation; remove the bearish bias immediately.
The second peak is considered approximately equal to the first if it is within a 3% price range of the first peak; reject patterns where the second peak exceeds this threshold upward.
